Ezhuthu Kamalam Multiscript Font Family
=======================================

![Five scripts, one aperture](proofs/kamalam_multiscript.png)

**Ezhuthu Kamalam** is a multiscript display type system built around one
idea: the counter as a **lotus gateway**. At one end of its variable axis a
loop is the classic round form; at the other, its crown rises into a soft
petal. The transformation is not a decorative filter — it is a real OpenType
variation axis, interpolated from point-compatible outlines.

The family began with Malayalam and now carries the same `APER` axis into
**Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali), Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**. Each
script is a separate variable family because its shaping, glyph set and
vertical metrics are its own; together they share one axis, one set of named
stops, one Spectrum palette and one build pipeline.

The Malayalam branch is built on the **Manjari** skeleton by Santhosh
Thottingal and Swathanthra Malayalam Computing. The four new branches are
built on the corresponding **Noto Sans** skeletons by the Noto Project
Authors. All bases are used under the SIL Open Font License. The aperture
engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are new work by
the Ezhuthu Project Authors.

Five Scripts, One Aperture
--------------------------

| Script | Family | Base skeleton | Script codepoints | Glyphs |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Malayalam | `Ezhuthu Kamalam` | Manjari | full block | 918 / 912 |
| Devanagari (Hindi) | `Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari` | Noto Sans Devanagari | 201 | 1117 |
| Tamil | `Ezhuthu Kamalam Tamil` | Noto Sans Tamil | 72 | 576 |
| Telugu | `Ezhuthu Kamalam Telugu` | Noto Sans Telugu | 100 | 1247 |
| Kannada | `Ezhuthu Kamalam Kannada` | Noto Sans Kannada | 91 | 933 |

“Hindi” is written in Devanagari; the Devanagari family also covers Marathi,
Nepali and Sanskrit. The Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families each cover their
own script plus the Latin, digits and punctuation inherited from the base.

![The APER axis across four scripts](proofs/kamalam_multiscript_axis.png)

Each script has its own aperture profile, because the scripts do not share a
single counter grammar:

- **Devanagari** keeps the shirorekha dead straight. An absolute freeze at the
  headline means only the counters and the loops below it open into petals.
- **Tamil** uses a gentler hole-and-crown profile. Its counters are fewer and
  more open, so the petal is concentrated in the loops and the inner curves.
- **Telugu** and **Kannada** take the full hole-and-crown warp. Their round
  loops carry the lotus form most naturally.
- The warp is restricted to the script's **GSUB closure**, so Latin,
  punctuation and unrelated glyphs remain in the base style. The axis changes
  the script's counters, never its glyph sequence, spacing or kerning.

The per-script specimens show the full system:

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Devanagari](proofs/kamalam_devanagari.png) | ![Tamil](proofs/kamalam_tamil.png) |
| ![Telugu](proofs/kamalam_telugu.png) | ![Kannada](proofs/kamalam_kannada.png) |

The Aperture Axis
-----------------

![The five stops of the aperture axis](proofs/kamalam_axis.png)

Every counter in Ezhuthu Kamalam can open from a classic round loop
(`APER 0`) to a pointed lotus gateway (`APER 100`). The axis is exposed as
`APER` in every variable font and has five named stops:

| APER | Name | Character |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Round | The classic loop |
| 25 | Quarter | A first lift at the crown |
| 50 | Bloom | The gateway begins to open |
| 75 | Three-quarters | A clear petal silhouette |
| 100 | Petal | The full lotus display cut (default) |

![The aperture axis in motion](proofs/kamalam_aper.gif)

The two masters share the same point topology, so every intermediate value is
a designed shape and HarfBuzz shaping is identical at every stop. The axis
changes the counters and crowns, never the glyph sequence, the spacing or the
kerning.

The Spectrum
------------

![Ezhuthu Kamalam Spectrum](proofs/kamalam_gradient.png)

**Ezhuthu Kamalam Spectrum** carries a blue → orange gradient inside the font
itself with COLRv1 and CPAL. Blue sits at the crown, orange near the baseline
and gold in the descenders, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field
rather than a set of separately coloured letters. Regular and Bold Spectrum
builds ship for every script.

The spectrum is an homage to the lotus-and-gateway visual language of
[Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand). This project is independent and is
not affiliated with or endorsed by Sarvam AI.

In Context
----------

The same fonts, the same axis, the same spectrum — applied to the kinds of
surfaces a contemporary Indian type system has to live on.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Poster](proofs/kamalam_poster.png) | ![Editorial spread](proofs/kamalam_editorial.png) |
| ![Product UI](proofs/kamalam_ui.png) | ![Social card](proofs/kamalam_social.png) |

![Ezhuthu Kamalam lockup](proofs/kamalam_lockup.png)

Character Set
-------------

![Ezhuthu Kamalam character sheet](proofs/kamalam_glyphs.png)

The Malayalam family covers the complete Malayalam block plus Latin:

- 36 consonants, 16 independent vowels, all vowel signs and chillus
- Common conjuncts, reph forms, ya/va post-base signs
- Malayalam digits ൦–൯ and historical numerals ൰–൵
- Rare letters (ഩ ഺ ഽ ൏), chandrabindu, visarga, virama
- Latin uppercase/lowercase, digits, punctuation and common accents
- **918 glyphs** in Regular, **912** in Bold

The multiscript families retain the full cmap and GSUB coverage of their
bases: Devanagari includes the Devanagari block, Devanagari Extended and the
Vedic extensions supported by Noto; Tamil, Telugu and Kannada include their
full blocks. Coverage is verified codepoint by codepoint in
`tests/test_multiscript.py`.

The Family
----------

The Malayalam family:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Regular.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Regular, `APER` 0–100 (default 100) |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Bold.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Bold, `APER` 0–100 (default 100) |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Spectrum.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Bold + COLRv1 spectrum |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-SpectrumRegular.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Regular + COLRv1 spectrum |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Round.ttf/.woff2` | Static `APER 0` instance |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-Petal.ttf/.woff2` | Static `APER 100` instance |
| `fonts/EzhuthuKamalam-BoldPetal.ttf/.woff2` | Static Bold `APER 100` instance |

Each new script ships the same seven styles:

| Family | Files |
|---|---|
| Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari | `fonts/EzhuthuKamalamDevanagari-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
| Ezhuthu Kamalam Tamil | `fonts/EzhuthuKamalamTamil-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
| Ezhuthu Kamalam Telugu | `fonts/EzhuthuKamalamTelugu-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
| Ezhuthu Kamalam Kannada | `fonts/EzhuthuKamalamKannada-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |

Specimens:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `specimen/index.html` | Interactive Malayalam specimen (fonts embedded) |
| `specimen/multiscript.html` | Interactive five-script specimen with a shared APER slider |
| `proofs/EzhuthuKamalam-Specimen.pdf` | Vector Malayalam PDF specimen |
| `proofs/EzhuthuKamalam-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf` | Vector multiscript PDF specimen |

Downloading the font files
--------------------------

The latest TTF and WOFF2 builds live in [`fonts/`](fonts/). The multiscript
specimen is [`specimen/multiscript.html`](specimen/multiscript.html); the
vector PDF is
[`proofs/EzhuthuKamalam-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf`](proofs/EzhuthuKamalam-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf).
Open the HTML directly, or serve both specimens with:

```bash
make serve   # http://localhost:8000
```

Using the font
--------------

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari";
  src: url("EzhuthuKamalamDevanagari-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400;
}

.deva {
  font-family: "Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari";
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100; /* 0 = round, 100 = petal */
}
```

```python
# HarfBuzz / uharfbuzz
font.set_variations({"APER": 65})
```

For mixed-script copy, stack the families. The browser picks the first family
that supports each character; the Malayalam family handles Malayalam and the
shared Latin, and the script families fill in the rest:

```css
.multiscript {
  font-family:
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam",
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari",
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam Tamil",
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam Telugu",
    "Ezhuthu Kamalam Kannada",
    sans-serif;
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
}
```

For the colour builds, use `EzhuthuKamalam<Script>-SpectrumRegular` or
`EzhuthuKamalam<Script>-Spectrum`. Clients with COLRv1 support paint the
gradient; clients without it fall back to the monochrome outlines.

Building from source
--------------------

The build is Python + fontTools + varLib + COLRv1:

```bash
make venv            # create .venv and install dependencies
make kamalam         # Malayalam: masters, variable fonts, Spectrum, instances
make multiscript     # Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families
make test            # shaping, variation and colour tests for all five scripts
make proofs          # specimen PNGs, GIF and both interactive HTML specimens
make pdf             # Malayalam vector PDF specimen
make pdf-multiscript # multiscript vector PDF specimen
make qa              # fontbakery on Malayalam Regular and Bold
make qa-multiscript  # fontbakery on the four new Regular/Bold families
```

Sources live in `sources/base/` (Manjari and the four Noto Sans variable
skeletons). The aperture engine is `tools/kamalam.py`; the multiscript driver
is `tools/multiscript.py`. The build is reproducible: repeated runs produce
byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. Design and engineering notes are in
[NOTES.md](NOTES.md).

Testing and QA
--------------

- HarfBuzz shaping across `APER 0`, `50` and `100` for every script — identical
  glyph sequences and advances, no `.notdef` in any test case.
- Full cmap coverage of each base script, plus conjuncts, matras, reph forms
  and the Devanagari Vedic extensions supported by the base.
- Outline variation at the two extremes, and a guard that Latin stays
  untouched in the script families.
- Static Round/Petal instances differ from each other and carry the correct
  names; COLRv1/CPAL paint graphs are present in every Spectrum build.
- Fontbakery universal: **0 FAIL** on all eight multiscript Regular/Bold
  variable fonts (the same documented custom-axis, STAT-name-length and
  Bold/`fsSelection` exclusions as Malayalam; inherited Noto warnings are
  listed in [NOTES.md](NOTES.md)).
- Both HTML specimens and the COLRv1 gradient were verified in headless
  Chromium 156; the shared APER slider drives all four script families.
- Byte-identical repeat builds for `make kamalam` and `make multiscript`.

License
-------

Ezhuthu Kamalam is licensed under the **SIL Open Font License v1.1**
(<http://scripts.sil.org/OFL>). See [OFL.txt](OFL.txt).

The Malayalam base skeleton is **Manjari**, Copyright 2018 The Manjari
Project Authors (<https://gitlab.com/smc/fonts/manjari>), under the SIL Open
Font License 1.1.

The Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada base skeletons are the **Noto Sans**
families, Copyright 2022 The Noto Project Authors
(<https://github.com/notofonts>), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. Their
upstream licences are kept in `sources/base/NotoSans*-OFL.txt`.

The aperture engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are
Copyright 2026 The Ezhuthu Project Authors.

The legacy v0.2 from-scratch parametric draft is preserved in
[`legacy/`](legacy/) and in `tools/glyphs_ml.py`.

Credits
-------

- **Design, aperture engine, variable fonts, Spectrum, specimens:** Ezhuthu
  Project Authors
- **Malayalam base skeleton:** Santhosh Thottingal and Swathanthra Malayalam
  Computing
- **Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada base skeletons:** The Noto Project
  Authors
- **Legacy v0.2 shaping engine:** adapted from
  [Nupuram](https://gitlab.com/smc/fonts/Nupuram) by Santhosh Thottingal / SMC
  (MIT)
- **Sarvam inspiration:** the blue → orange spectrum and the gateway/lotus
  language are an homage to [Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand)

Getting involved
----------------

Bug reports, glyph requests and feature suggestions are welcome. Open an
issue in the repository or send a pull request against the `tools/` and
`sources/` directories. Please run `make test` and `make qa-multiscript`
before sending a contribution.

If you use Ezhuthu Kamalam in a project, a small credit — “Typeface: Ezhuthu
Kamalam” — is appreciated.

`tests/test_kamalam.py` checks:

- `fvar` axis `APER = 0…100`, default 100;

- the OFL name table and Manjari attribution on every build;

  glyph sequences;
- coverage of every assigned Malayalam codepoint;
- outline variation between the extremes;
- COLR/CPAL structure, 907 paint records and 7 palette entries.

The HTML specimen was also checked in headless Chromium 156: the embedded
variable fonts load, the APER slider changes the live instance, and the
`Ezhuthu Kamalam Spectrum` sample paints its COLRv1 gradient in the browser.

Builds are reproducible: `head.created`/`head.modified` are pinned to a fixed
date and `recalcTimestamp` is disabled, so repeated `make kamalam` runs produce
byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. `make proofs` is deterministic too.

The old `tests/test_font.py` still covers the legacy draft.

## 7. Fontbakery notes

The Regular font passes `fontbakery check-universal` with two exclusions that
do not apply to this design:

- `opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct` assumes a registered `wght`/`wdth`
  axis; Ezhuthu Kamalam's only axis is the custom `APER`.
- `alt_caron` is a Czech/Slovak-specific check that wants `ď` to use a
  non-standard caron glyph. The Latin `ď` here uses a combining caron, which
  is typographically correct; the check is not relevant to a Malayalam face.

For the Bold and Spectrum builds, `opentype/fsselection` and
`opentype/mac_style` also need excluding because fontbakery infers "Bold"
from a `wght` axis or a filename convention and cannot see the custom-axis
Bold style; the OS/2 and `head` values themselves are correct. Run the QA
target with:

```bash
make qa
```

The specimen HTML and COLRv1 paint were verified in headless Chromium 156.

## 8. Known limits / next work

- The transform is derived from Manjari's skeleton; it is not a new
  construction from a blank page. A future release could redraw the skeleton
  from the same aperture grammar while keeping the axis.
- The Spectrum gradient is static; a `COLRv1` variable gradient tied to `APER`
  would be the next step.
- A `wght` axis would need point-compatible masters from a variable source
  (Noto Sans Malayalam is a candidate) or a carefully offset master.
- The display cut is optimised for large sizes. A text-optimised cut with
  smaller petal lifts and looser spacing is planned.

## 8. Known limits / next work

- The transform is derived from Manjari's skeleton; it is not a new
  construction from a blank page. A future release could redraw the skeleton
  from the same aperture grammar while keeping the axis.
- The Spectrum gradient is static; a `COLRv1` variable gradient tied to `APER`
  would be the next step.
- A `wght` axis would need point-compatible masters from a variable source
  (Noto Sans Malayalam is a candidate) or a carefully offset master.
- The display cut is optimised for large sizes. A text-optimised cut with
  smaller petal lifts and looser spacing is planned.

## 9. The multiscript extension

### 9.1 Why separate families

Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face; it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
Kannada glyphs. A literal Manjari derivative therefore cannot cover those
scripts. The multiscript release uses one OFL skeleton per script and keeps the
same derivative model: rename, preserve the upstream copyright, record the
base, and do the new work in the aperture engine, axis, Spectrum, metrics and
specimens.

The four new families are deliberately separate variable fonts rather than one
merged font. Scripts have different GSUB/GPOS tables, glyph names, mark
attachments and vertical metrics; merging them would create conflicts in
shared Latin, punctuation and mark glyphs. Separate families also match how
Anek, Noto and most multiscript systems ship, and let each script keep its own
line height.

### 9.2 Sources

| Branch | Base | Upstream |
|---|---|---|
| Devanagari | Noto Sans Devanagari VF | notofonts/devanagari |
| Tamil | Noto Sans Tamil VF | notofonts/tamil |
| Telugu | Noto Sans Telugu VF | notofonts/telugu |
| Kannada | Noto Sans Kannada VF | notofonts/kannada |

The variable bases are instantiated at `wght=400/700`, `wdth=100`, scaled to
1000 UPM (they are already 1000), stripped of hinting and variation tables, and
given the Ezhuthu name/metrics. The vendored files and SHA-256 checksums are in
`sources/base/README.md`.

### 9.3 Script-specific aperture profiles

The warp is still point-preserving, but the profiles differ because the
scripts do not share one counter grammar.

| Script | hole_bump | peak_bump | freeze | sigma_f | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| Devanagari | 110 | 60 | absolute y=545, fade 120 | 0.22 | Keeps the shirorekha straight; only loops below it open |
| Tamil | 100 | 25 | top 18% | 0.30 | Gentler; concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
| Telugu | 110 | 40 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |
| Kannada | 110 | 36 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |

`PETAL_WARP` now supports `only` (a glyph-name set), `freeze_top` (fraction),
`freeze_above` (absolute y), `freeze_fade`, `peak_max_frac`/`peak_max_y` and
`valley_bump`. With the defaults these are no-ops, which is why the Malayalam
build remains byte-identical.

The **absolute freeze** is the important Devanagari detail. Devanagari base
letters share a headline at roughly y=570–622; freezing above y=545 leaves the
headline and its junctions untouched, while the counter tops below 545 can
rise. A 120-unit fade avoids a hard step at the freeze boundary. The first
attempt used a per-glyph percentage freeze and a wide Gaussian, which pulled
the headline at the stem junctions; the absolute freeze plus a narrower
`sigma_f=0.22` fixed it.

### 9.4 Glyph filtering

`petal_warp` accepts `only`, a set of glyph names. `tools/multiscript.py`
computes that set with `fontTools.subset`: it starts from the script's
codepoints and closes over GSUB, so conjuncts, half forms, reph forms,
contextual variants and matras are included. Latin, punctuation and unrelated
glyphs are left in the base style. This is why the Latin in the new families
stays Noto Sans, while the script outline changes.

The closure sizes (excluding `.notdef`) are 735 Devanagari, 166 Tamil, 723
Telugu and 414 Kannada glyphs.

### 9.5 Metrics

FONTLOG for Ezhuthu Kamalam
==========================

Ezhuthu Kamalam is an aperture-variable Malayalam display family. It is based
on the Manjari skeleton (OFL 1.1) and adds a new Petal/Aperture transformation,
a variable APER axis, and a COLRv1 blue→orange Spectrum build.

2026-11-09 — v1.000 (Kamalam)
-----------------------------

@@ -87,14 +87,27 @@ def _split_contours(glyph):

-               sigma_f=SIGMA_F, pinch=PINCH, cap_frac=CAP_FRAC):

     """Move counters and outer crowns into lotus-petal shapes.

   But note: bumping version and URL changes Malayalam fonts, which are not in this commit yet. If we commit code only, the working tree still has modified Malayalam fonts; the commit is buildable and tests pass. The version bump code affects future builds. Fine.
   - However, commit 1 includes `set_metrics` version bump to 1.100; the existing fonts in the commit are still v1.000 until the font commit. That's okay, but if someone checks out commit 1, `make kamalam` produces v1.100 fonts; the committed fonts don't match the code. Atomic commits ideally should include generated outputs. Since we commit fonts separately, there will be intermediate states where code and binaries mismatch. To keep atomicity, maybe commit **code + regenerated Malayalam fonts** together as "build: generalize the aperture engine and bump Malayalam to v1.100". Then commit the multiscript pipeline separately, then each script's fonts. This is coherent:

     - Commit 2: `tools/multiscript.py` pipeline + tests? Tests require fonts. Could commit pipeline alone; no fonts.
     - Commit 3-6: each script's fonts.

   But `Makefile` references `tests/test_multiscript.py` and `multiscript`; if committed at the end, fine.

Let's inspect all `Kamalam`/`kamalam`/`Ezhuthu` occurrences in current tools/docs after the changes (using `git grep` again but exclude generated HTML). We saw the remaining. Fix them with targeted edits.

#### Makefile rename

Current makefile.

.PHONY: help venv kamalam multiscript legacy test proofs specimen serve clean distclean \
	pdf pdf-multiscript qa qa-multiscript

PY := .venv/bin/python
PIP := .venv/bin/pip

help:
	@echo "targets:"
	@echo "  venv      create .venv and install build/proof dependencies"
	@echo "  kamalam   build the variable Kallar family + Spectrum"
	@echo "  multiscript build Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families"
	@echo "  legacy    rebuild the v0.2 parametric draft (legacy/fonts)"
	@echo "  test      run shaping, variation and colour tests"
	@echo "  proofs    render the specimen PNGs and the HTML specimen"
	@echo "  pdf       print the specimen to proofs/Kallar-Specimen.pdf"
	@echo "  pdf-multiscript print the multiscript specimen to PDF"
	@echo "  qa        run fontbakery on the Malayalam Regular and Bold"
	@echo "  qa-multiscript run fontbakery on the four script families"
	@echo "  specimen  alias for proofs"
	@echo "  serve     serve specimen/ on http://localhost:8000"
	@echo "  clean     remove generated UFOs and masters"
	@echo "  distclean remove generated fonts and proofs too"

venv:
	test -d .venv || { python3 -m venv .venv; $(PIP) install -U pip; }
	$(PIP) install -q ufoLib2 ufo2ft fonttools fontFeatures munch PyYAML \
		uharfbuzz freetype-py pillow booleanOperations Brotli scipy

kamalam: venv
	$(PY) tools/kallar.py all

multiscript: venv
	$(PY) tools/multiscript.py

legacy: venv
	$(PY) tools/build.py

test: venv kamalam multiscript
	$(PY) tests/test_kallar.py
	$(PY) tests/test_multiscript.py
	@if test -f legacy/fonts/Ezhuthu-Regular.ttf; then \
		$(PY) tests/test_font.py legacy/fonts/Ezhuthu-Regular.ttf; \
	else \
		echo "legacy font not built; run: make legacy"; \
	fi

proofs: kamalam multiscript
	$(PY) tools/specimen.py
	$(PY) tools/specimen_multiscript.py
	$(PY) tools/specimen_html.py
	$(PY) tools/specimen_multiscript_html.py

pdf: proofs
	$(PIP) install -q playwright
	$(PY) -m playwright install chromium
	$(PY) tools/pdf.py

pdf-multiscript: proofs
	$(PIP) install -q playwright
	$(PY) -m playwright install chromium
	$(PY) tools/pdf.py specimen/multiscript.html \
		proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf

qa: kamalam
	$(PIP) install -q fontbakery
	$(PY) -m fontbakery check-universal fonts/Kallar-Regular.ttf \
		--no-progress -x opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct -x alt_caron
	$(PY) -m fontbakery check-universal fonts/Kallar-Bold.ttf \
		--no-progress -x opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct -x alt_caron \
		-x opentype/fsselection -x opentype/mac_style

qa-multiscript: multiscript
	$(PIP) install -q fontbakery
	@for f in \
		fonts/KallarDevanagari-Regular.ttf \
		fonts/KallarDevanagari-Bold.ttf \
		fonts/KallarTamil-Regular.ttf \
		fonts/KallarTamil-Bold.ttf \
		fonts/KallarTelugu-Regular.ttf \
		fonts/KallarTelugu-Bold.ttf \
		fonts/KallarKannada-Regular.ttf \
		fonts/KallarKannada-Bold.ttf; do \
		echo "== $$f"; \
		$(PY) -m fontbakery check-universal "$$f" --no-progress \
			-x opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct -x alt_caron \
			-x opentype/fsselection -x opentype/mac_style \
			2>&1 | grep -E '^    (FAIL|WARN|PASS):|^Total:' | tail -5; \
	done

specimen: proofs
	@echo "open specimen/index.html in a browser (or run: make serve)"

serve: specimen
	$(PY) -m http.server 8000 --directory specimen

clean:
	rm -rf sources/ufo sources/masters

distclean: clean
	rm -rf fonts/*.ttf fonts/*.otf fonts/*.woff2 proofs/kallar_*.png \

FONTLOG for Ezhuthu Kamalam
==========================

Ezhuthu Kamalam is an aperture-variable multiscript display family. The
Malayalam branch is based on the Manjari skeleton (OFL 1.1); the Devanagari,
Tamil, Telugu and Kannada branches are based on the corresponding Noto Sans
skeletons (OFL 1.1). All branches add the Petal/Aperture transformation, a
variable APER axis, and COLRv1 blue→orange Spectrum builds.

2026-11-09 — v1.100 (Multiscript)
--------------------------------
- Added Ezhuthu Kamalam Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada.
- Each family: variable Regular and Bold with APER 0–100, static Round/Petal/
  Bold Petal instances, and COLRv1 Spectrum Regular/Bold builds.
- Same point-preserving aperture engine, with script-specific profiles:
  Devanagari absolute headline freeze; Tamil gentle profile; Telugu and
  Kannada full loop warp.
- Script glyph sets computed through the GSUB closure so Latin stays in the
  base style.
- Devanagari metrics: typo 1000/-408, win 1397/580 (Regular), 1398/597 (Bold).
  Tamil/Telugu/Kannada keep their base typographic ascenders and auto win
  metrics.
- New multiscript specimen (HTML + vector PDF), axis grid, hero poster and
  four script sheets.
- Tests: axes, metadata, shaping across APER, cmap coverage, outline
  variation, Latin guard, static instances and COLRv1 for all four scripts.
- Fontbakery: 0 FAIL on the eight new Regular/Bold VFs with the documented
  custom-axis / STAT-length / Bold exclusions.

2026-11-09 — v1.000 (Kamalam)
-----------------------------
- First production release of Ezhuthu Kamalam.
- Variable Regular and Bold fonts with the custom APER (Aperture) axis,
  0 = round, 50 = bloom, 100 = petal (default).
- Point-compatible masters generated by a capped petal warp; static Round,
  Petal and Bold Petal instances included.
- Ezhuthu Kamalam Spectrum: COLRv1/CPAL blue→orange gradient builds in
  Regular (913 colour glyphs) and Bold (907 colour glyphs), both with a
  7-colour palette.
- 1000 UPM, full Malayalam block + Latin, Manjari GSUB/GPOS preserved.
- New metrics: typo 800/-300, win 1100/700, USE_TYPO_METRICS.
- Self-contained HTML specimen, hero/axis/gradient/glyph-sheet PNG proofs.
- Tests: axes, shaping across APER, coverage, colour tables, legacy draft.

2023-?? — v0.2 (legacy draft)
-----------------------------
- Metric correction, letterform tuning, OTF/WOFF2 output, Makefile.
- Full Malayalam block coverage and working OpenType shaping.

2023-?? — v0.1 (legacy draft)
-----------------------------
- Initial from-scratch parametric Malayalam typeface: exact outline
  primitives, UFO generation, GSUB/GPOS via the vendored Nupuram engine.

License
-------
SIL Open Font License 1.1. See OFL.txt.
Malayalam base: Manjari, Copyright 2018 The Manjari Project Authors.
Multiscript bases: Noto Sans Devanagari/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada, Copyright 2022
The Noto Project Authors. Upstream licences are in sources/base/.

content.text:
These are display words in sample images. The font is Kallar, but the Malayalam word "കമലം" (lotus) is a design sample; it can stay as a word, not the brand. The user asked rename the font, not remove the word "lotus" from sample text. However, the brand name in the UI mockup "എഴുത്ത്" and the hero "എഴുത്ത് കമലം" should change to "കല്ലർ". Let's decide: - `tools/specimen.py` line 304 `word = "കമലം"` is the hero word (lotus); it's a specimen word, fine. But the brand is Kallar; the hero could show "കല്ലർ" instead. The word "കമലം" literally means lotus, which is the design concept; keeping it is nice. The font name is Kallar, but the sample can be "കമലം". No need to change. - Line 545 paragraph "എഴുത്ത് കമലം ഈ ലിപിക്ക്..." is the old brand in prose; change to "കല്ലർ ഈ ലിപിക്ക്...". - Line 587 hero gradient "എഴുത്ത്" (writing) is a word; could stay, but it was the old brand first word. Change to "കല്ലർ" for brand consistency. - Line 610 UI mockup "എഴുത്ത്" (writing) as product name; change to "കല്ലർ". - Line 650 UI card "കമലം" (lotus) as sample; fine. - Line 674 lockup "എഴുത്ത് കമലം" → "കല്ലർ". - `tools/specimen_html.py` line 329 hero `

കമലം

Change to "കല്ലർ" to reflect the brand. The line 406 "കമലം സർവം" is a spectrum sample; "lotus" + "all" is a phrase; could stay. But if the font is Kallar, "കമലം സർവം" still makes sense as a sample ("lotus is everything"). Keep or change? The brand rename should be visible. Use "കല്ലർ" in the hero, keep the spectrum sample as "കമലം സർവം" (design sample). Hmm, "Kallar" in Malayalam is "കല്ലർ"; the hero word would be the brand. Let's change the hero h1 to "കല്ലർ" and the UI footer big to "കല്ലർ". The spectrum sample "കമലം സർവം" can stay as a phrase; but it may confuse. Maybe change to "കല്ലർ സർവം" ("Kallar is everything")? That's odd. """Kallar — the aperture-variable Malayalam display family.

Design idea
-----------
Every Malayalam loop/arch is treated as a *gateway*: a round base that rises
to a soft lotus-petal crown.  The transformation is parametric and applied to
a proven open-source Malayalam skeleton (Manjari by Santhosh Thottingal /
SMC, OFL-1.1).  It is exposed as the ``APER`` (Aperture) variation axis:

without copying its wordmark.

points, so varLib can interpolate between them cleanly.

def script_codepoints(font, ranges):
    cps = set()
    for table in font["cmap"].tables:
        if not table.isUnicode():
            continue
        for cp in table.cmap:
            if any(lo <= cp <= hi for lo, hi in ranges):
                cps.add(cp)
    return cps


def script_glyphs(path, codepoints):
    """Return the GSUB closure of a script's codepoints.

    Using fontTools' subsetter closure means conjuncts, half forms, reph forms
    and contextual variants are all included, while Latin, punctuation and
    unrelated glyphs are left in the base style.
    """
    font = TTFont(path)
    opts = subset.Options()
    opts.layout_features = ["*"]
    opts.notdef_outline = True
    opts.recalc_bounds = False
    opts.drop_tables = []
    subsetter = subset.Subsetter(opts)
    subsetter.populate(unicodes=codepoints)
    subsetter.subset(font)
    names = set(font.getGlyphOrder())
    names.discard(".notdef")
    return names

def script_codepoints(font, ranges):
    cps = set()
    for table in font["cmap"].tables:
        if not table.isUnicode():
            continue
        for cp in table.cmap:
            if any(lo <= cp <= hi for lo, hi in ranges):
                cps.add(cp)
    return cps


def script_glyphs(path, codepoints):
    """Return the GSUB closure of a script's codepoints.

    Using fontTools' subsetter closure means conjuncts, half forms, reph forms
    and contextual variants are all included, while Latin, punctuation and
    unrelated glyphs are left in the base style.
    """
    font = TTFont(path)
    opts = subset.Options()
    opts.layout_features = ["*"]
    opts.notdef_outline = True
    opts.recalc_bounds = False
    opts.drop_tables = []
    subsetter = subset.Subsetter(opts)
    subsetter.populate(unicodes=codepoints)
    subsetter.subset(font)
    names = set(font.getGlyphOrder())
    names.discard(".notdef")
    return names

Kallar Multiscript Font Family
=======================================

![Five scripts, one aperture](proofs/kallar_multiscript.png)

**Kallar** is a multiscript display type system built around one
idea: the counter as a **lotus gateway**. At one end of its variable axis a
loop is the classic round form; at the other, its crown rises into a soft
petal. The transformation is not a decorative filter — it is a real OpenType
variation axis, interpolated from point-compatible outlines.

The family began with Malayalam and now carries the same `APER` axis into
**Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali), Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**. Each
script is a separate variable family because its shaping, glyph set and
vertical metrics are its own; together they share one axis, one set of named
stops, one Spectrum palette and one build pipeline.

The Malayalam branch is built on the **Manjari** skeleton by Santhosh
Thottingal and Swathanthra Malayalam Computing. The four new branches are
built on the corresponding **Noto Sans** skeletons by the Noto Project
Authors. All bases are used under the SIL Open Font License. The aperture
engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are new work by
the Kallar Project Authors.

Five Scripts, One Aperture
--------------------------

| Script | Family | Base skeleton | Script codepoints | Glyphs |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Malayalam | `Kallar` | Manjari | full block | 918 / 912 |
| Devanagari (Hindi) | `Kallar Devanagari` | Noto Sans Devanagari | 201 | 1117 |
| Tamil | `Kallar Tamil` | Noto Sans Tamil | 72 | 576 |
| Telugu | `Kallar Telugu` | Noto Sans Telugu | 100 | 1247 |
| Kannada | `Kallar Kannada` | Noto Sans Kannada | 91 | 933 |

“Hindi” is written in Devanagari; the Devanagari family also covers Marathi,
Nepali and Sanskrit. The Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families each cover their
own script plus the Latin, digits and punctuation inherited from the base.

![The APER axis across four scripts](proofs/kallar_multiscript_axis.png)

Each script has its own aperture profile, because the scripts do not share a
single counter grammar:

- **Devanagari** keeps the shirorekha dead straight. An absolute freeze at the
  headline means only the counters and the loops below it open into petals.
- **Tamil** uses a gentler hole-and-crown profile. Its counters are fewer and
  more open, so the petal is concentrated in the loops and the inner curves.
- **Telugu** and **Kannada** take the full hole-and-crown warp. Their round
  loops carry the lotus form most naturally.
- The warp is restricted to the script's **GSUB closure**, so Latin,
  punctuation and unrelated glyphs remain in the base style. The axis changes
  the script's counters, never its glyph sequence, spacing or kerning.

The per-script specimens show the full system:

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Devanagari](proofs/kallar_devanagari.png) | ![Tamil](proofs/kallar_tamil.png) |
| ![Telugu](proofs/kallar_telugu.png) | ![Kannada](proofs/kallar_kannada.png) |

The Aperture Axis
-----------------

![The five stops of the aperture axis](proofs/kallar_axis.png)

Every counter in Kallar can open from a classic round loop
(`APER 0`) to a pointed lotus gateway (`APER 100`). The axis is exposed as
`APER` in every variable font and has five named stops:

| APER | Name | Character |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Round | The classic loop |
| 25 | Quarter | A first lift at the crown |
| 50 | Bloom | The gateway begins to open |
| 75 | Three-quarters | A clear petal silhouette |
| 100 | Petal | The full lotus display cut (default) |

![The aperture axis in motion](proofs/kallar_aper.gif)

- Both HTML specimens and the COLRv1 gradient were verified in headless
  Chromium 156; the shared APER slider drives all four script families.
- Byte-identical repeat builds for `make kallar` and `make multiscript`.

License
-------

Kallar is licensed under the **SIL Open Font License v1.1**
(<http://scripts.sil.org/OFL>). See [OFL.txt](OFL.txt).

The Malayalam base skeleton is **Manjari**, Copyright 2018 The Manjari
Project Authors (<https://gitlab.com/smc/fonts/manjari>), under the SIL Open
Font License 1.1.

The Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada base skeletons are the **Noto Sans**
families, Copyright 2022 The Noto Project Authors
(<https://github.com/notofonts>), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. Their
upstream licences are kept in `sources/base/NotoSans*-OFL.txt`.

The aperture engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are
Copyright 2026 The Kallar Project Authors.

The legacy v0.2 from-scratch parametric draft is preserved in
[`legacy/`](legacy/) and in `tools/glyphs_ml.py`.

Credits
-------

- **Design, aperture engine, variable fonts, Spectrum, specimens:** Kallar

- **Malayalam base skeleton:** Santhosh Thottingal and Swathanthra Malayalam

- **Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada base skeletons:** The Noto Project

- **Sarvam inspiration:** the blue → orange spectrum and the gateway/lotus

Getting involved
----------------

Bug reports, glyph requests and feature suggestions are welcome. Open an
issue in the repository or send a pull request against the `tools/` and
`sources/` directories. Please run `make test` and `make qa-multiscript`
before sending a contribution.

If you use Kallar in a project, a small credit — “Typeface: Kallar” — is
appreciated.

# Kallar — design & engineering notes

## 1. The idea

Malayalam is a loop script. The loop head (തല) is the script's most recognisable
gesture: a round counter, an opening, a tail. Most Malayalam typefaces treat
that loop as a circle or an oval. Kallar treats it as a **gateway**.

At `APER 0` the counter is the classic round loop inherited from Manjari. As
`APER` rises, the crown of the counter lifts into a soft point: the negative
space becomes a lotus petal / a temple doorway. The outer silhouette follows
with a gentler version of the same gesture, so open arches (മ, ന, ത) and closed
loops (ക, ഖ, ങ) share one rhythm. The result is not a decorative overlay; the
*counters themselves* change shape.

The second layer is colour. Sarvam's identity uses a blue → orange spectrum and
a lotus/gateway monogram. Kallar Spectrum carries a vertical
blue → orange gradient inside the font with COLRv1, clipped to each glyph. At
text sizes the tops are blue, the baseline zone is pink/orange and the
descenders are gold — one continuous field across the text block.

The family is deliberately a **display** companion, not a replacement for a
text face. It is designed to be set large, where the petal crowns and the
spectrum are visible.

## 2. Why Manjari is the skeleton

The project's first two versions attempted a fully from-scratch parametric
Malayalam design (`legacy/`, `tools/glyphs_ml.py`). That work proved the
pipeline and the shaping stack, but matching the structural subtlety of a
production Malayalam face — the exact placement of loops, the counter rhythm,
the conjunct grammar — is a years-long project. For the production release we
made a deliberate choice:

- use **Manjari** (SIL OFL 1.1, by Santhosh Thottingal / SMC) as the
  structural foundation, because its loops and proportions are already a
  high-quality expression of the script;
- keep the base unmodified in `sources/base/` and record the transformation in
  code;

# Kallar

### A multiscript typeface that blooms.

![Kallar — five scripts, one aperture](proofs/kallar_multiscript.png)

![License: OFL 1.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-OFL%201.1-ee7944)
![Scripts: 5](https://img.shields.io/badge/scripts-5-3d4fbf)
![Variable: APER 0–100](https://img.shields.io/badge/variable-APER%200--100-7f63d6)
![Colour: COLRv1](https://img.shields.io/badge/colour-COLRv1-d973a0)

**Kallar** is a multiscript display type system built around one idea: the
counter as a **lotus gateway**. At one end of its variable axis a loop is the
classic round form; at the other, its crown rises into a soft petal. The
transformation is not a decorative filter — it is a real OpenType variation
axis, interpolated from point-compatible outlines.

The family began with Malayalam and now carries the same `APER` axis into
**Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali), Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**. Each
script is a separate variable family because its shaping, glyph set and
vertical metrics are its own; together they share one axis, one set of design
stops, one Spectrum palette and one build pipeline.

The Malayalam branch is built on the **Manjari** skeleton by Santhosh
Thottingal and Swathanthra Malayalam Computing. The four new branches are
built on the corresponding **Noto Sans** skeletons by the Noto Project
Authors. All bases are used under the SIL Open Font License. The aperture
engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are new work by
the Kallar Project Authors.

Kallar lives at
[github.com/kurianbenoy/kallar](https://github.com/kurianbenoy/kallar).

---

## Contents

- [The idea](#the-idea)
- [Five scripts, one aperture](#five-scripts-one-aperture)
- [The APER axis](#the-aper-axis)
- [The Spectrum](#the-spectrum)
- [In context](#in-context)
- [Character set](#character-set)
- [The family](#the-family)
- [Download](#download)
- [Using Kallar](#using-kallar)
- [Building from source](#building-from-source)
- [Testing and QA](#testing-and-qa)
- [Design notes](#design-notes)
- [License](#license)
- [Credits](#credits)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [Version history](#version-history)

---

## The idea

Malayalam is a script of loops. The loop head is its most recognisable
gesture: a round counter, an opening, a tail. Most typefaces treat that loop
as a circle or an oval. Kallar treats it as a **gateway**.

At `APER 0` the counter is a classic round loop. As `APER` rises, the crown of
the counter lifts into a soft point: the negative space becomes a lotus petal,
a temple doorway. The outer silhouette follows with a gentler version of the
same gesture, so open arches and closed loops share one rhythm. The counters
themselves change shape — this is outline variation, not a decorative overlay.

The second layer is colour. **Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange
gradient inside the font with COLRv1 and CPAL. The gradient is defined once per
glyph in font units, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than
a set of separately coloured letters.

Kallar is a **display** companion, designed to be set large where the petal
crowns and the spectrum are visible. It is also comfortable in short text,
where the crowns settle into a quiet, readable rhythm.

### Design principles

1. **The counter is the signature.** The transform starts in the negative
   space, not on the outer contour.
2. **One grammar, five scripts.** Scripts keep their own shaping and
   proportions, but share the same aperture logic.
3. **Point compatibility over effects.** Masters only move existing points, so
   every intermediate value is a designed shape and text keeps its metrics.
4. **Colour is part of the type.** The spectrum is painted by the font, not
   pasted on top of it.
5. **Honest derivatives.** The base skeletons, their authors and their OFL
   licences are recorded in the fonts and in this repository.

---

## Five scripts, one aperture

| Script | Family | Base skeleton | Script codepoints | Glyphs |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Malayalam | `Kallar` | Manjari | full block | 918 / 912 |
| Devanagari (Hindi) | `Kallar Devanagari` | Noto Sans Devanagari | 201 | 1117 |
| Tamil | `Kallar Tamil` | Noto Sans Tamil | 72 | 576 |
| Telugu | `Kallar Telugu` | Noto Sans Telugu | 100 | 1247 |
| Kannada | `Kallar Kannada` | Noto Sans Kannada | 91 | 933 |

“Hindi” is written in Devanagari; the Devanagari family also covers Marathi,
Nepali and Sanskrit. The Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families each cover their
own script plus the Latin, digits and punctuation inherited from the base.

![The APER axis across four scripts](proofs/kallar_multiscript_axis.png)

### Script-specific profiles

Each script has its own aperture profile, because the scripts do not share a
single counter grammar:

- **Devanagari** keeps the shirorekha dead straight. An absolute freeze at the
  headline means only the counters and the loops below it open into petals.
- **Tamil** uses a gentler hole-and-crown profile. Its counters are fewer and
  more open, so the petal is concentrated in the loops and inner curves.
- **Telugu** and **Kannada** take the full hole-and-crown warp. Their round
  loops carry the lotus form most naturally.
- The warp is restricted to the script's **GSUB closure**, so Latin,
  punctuation and unrelated glyphs remain in the base style. The axis changes
  the script's counters, never its glyph sequence, spacing or kerning.

The per-script specimens show the full system:

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Devanagari](proofs/kallar_devanagari.png) | ![Tamil](proofs/kallar_tamil.png) |
| ![Telugu](proofs/kallar_telugu.png) | ![Kannada](proofs/kallar_kannada.png) |

---

## The APER axis

![The five stops of the aperture axis](proofs/kallar_axis.png)

Every counter in Kallar can open from a classic round loop (`APER 0`) to a
pointed lotus gateway (`APER 100`). The axis has five design stops:

| APER | Name | Character |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Round | The classic loop |
| 25 | Quarter | A first lift at the crown |
| 50 | Bloom | The gateway begins to open |
| 75 | Three-quarters | A clear petal silhouette |
| 100 | Petal | The full lotus display cut (default) |

![The aperture axis in motion](proofs/kallar_aper.gif)

The two masters share the same point topology, so every intermediate value is
a designed shape and HarfBuzz shaping is identical at every stop. The axis
changes the counters and crowns, never the glyph sequence, the spacing or the
kerning.

```css
/* 0 = round · 50 = bloom · 100 = petal */
font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
```

---

## The Spectrum

![Kallar Spectrum](proofs/kallar_gradient.png)

**Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange gradient inside the font itself
with COLRv1 and CPAL. Blue sits at the crown, orange near the baseline and gold
in the descenders, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than a
set of separately coloured letters. Regular and Bold Spectrum builds ship for
every script.

| Stop | Colour | Role |
|---:|---|---|
| 0.00 | `#181E5C` | deep indigo |
| 0.20 | `#2B3FB0` | blue |
| 0.40 | `#5C64DB` | periwinkle |
| 0.58 | `#A06CD2` | violet |
| 0.74 | `#D973A0` | pink |
| 0.88 | `#EE7944` | Sarvam orange |
| 1.00 | `#F9C36D` | warm gold |

Clients with COLRv1 support paint the gradient; clients without it fall back
to the monochrome outlines. The gradient is clipped to each glyph outline and
runs from `y=620` to `y=-120` in font units.

The spectrum is an homage to the lotus-and-gateway visual language of
[Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand). This project is independent and is
not affiliated with or endorsed by Sarvam AI.

surfaces a contemporary Indian type system has to live on.

## Character set

![Kallar character sheet](proofs/kallar_glyphs.png)

The Malayalam family covers the complete Malayalam block plus Latin:

- 36 consonants, 16 independent vowels, all vowel signs and chillus
- Common conjuncts, reph forms, ya/va post-base signs
- Malayalam digits ൦–൯ and historical numerals ൰–൵
- Rare letters (ഩ ഺ ഽ ൏), chandrabindu, visarga, virama
- Latin uppercase/lowercase, digits, punctuation and common accents
- **918 glyphs** in Regular, **912** in Bold

The multiscript families retain the full cmap and GSUB coverage of their
bases: Devanagari includes the Devanagari block, Devanagari Extended and the
Vedic extensions supported by Noto; Tamil, Telugu and Kannada include their
full blocks. Coverage is verified codepoint by codepoint in
`tests/test_multiscript.py`.

| Family | Script cmap | Colour glyphs (Spectrum) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Kallar (Malayalam) | full block | 913 Regular / 907 Bold |
| Kallar Devanagari | 201 | 1111 |
| Kallar Tamil | 72 | 570 |
| Kallar Telugu | 100 | 1242 |
| Kallar Kannada | 91 | 928 |

## Download

The latest TTF and WOFF2 builds live in [`fonts/`](fonts/). The multiscript
specimen is [`specimen/multiscript.html`](specimen/multiscript.html); the
vector PDF is
[`proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf`](proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf).
Open the HTML directly, or serve both specimens with:

```bash
make serve   # http://localhost:8000
```

For most web projects, use the WOFF2 variable fonts. For desktop design apps,
install the TTF variable fonts. If an app does not expose custom variation
axes, use the static `Round` (APER 0) or `Petal` (APER 100) instances.

> **Note:** the five script families are deliberately separate fonts. There is

## Using Kallar

### Web

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Kallar";
  src: url("Kallar-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400;
  font-display: swap;
}

@font-face {
  font-family: "Kallar";
  src: url("Kallar-Bold.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 700;
  font-display: swap;
}

.bloom {
  font-family: "Kallar";
  font-weight: 700;
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100; /* 0 = round, 100 = petal */
}
```

### Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
  src: url("KallarDevanagari-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400;
}

.deva {
  font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
}
```

### Mixed-script copy

Stack the families. The browser picks the first family that supports each
character — the Malayalam family handles Malayalam and the shared Latin, and
the script families fill in the rest:

```css
.multiscript {
  font-family:
    "Kallar",
    "Kallar Devanagari",
    "Kallar Tamil",
    "Kallar Telugu",
    "Kallar Kannada",
    sans-serif;
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
}
```

### Colour

Use `Kallar-SpectrumRegular` / `Kallar-Spectrum`, or the corresponding
`Kallar<Script>-Spectrum*` builds. Clients with COLRv1 support paint the
gradient; clients without it fall back to the monochrome outlines.

```css
.spectrum {
  font-family: "Kallar Spectrum", "Kallar", sans-serif;
  font-weight: 700;
}
```

### JavaScript

```js
const title = document.querySelector(".bloom");
title.style.fontVariationSettings = '"APER" 65';
```

### HarfBuzz

```python
import uharfbuzz as hb

blob = hb.Blob.from_file_path("KallarDevanagari-Regular.ttf")
face = hb.Face(blob)
font = hb.Font(face)
font.set_variations({"APER": 65})
```

### The APER value

| Value | Use it for |
|---:|---|
| 0 | A conventional, round text cut |
| 25–50 | A subtle display lift |
| 50–75 | A clear petal silhouette |
| 100 | The full lotus display cut (default) |

## Building from source

The build is Python + fontTools + varLib + COLRv1.

```bash
make venv            # create .venv and install dependencies
make kallar          # Malayalam: masters, variable fonts, Spectrum, instances
make multiscript     # Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families
make test            # shaping, variation and colour tests for all five scripts
make proofs          # specimen PNGs, GIF and both interactive HTML specimens
make pdf             # Malayalam vector PDF specimen
make pdf-multiscript # multiscript vector PDF specimen
make qa              # fontbakery on Malayalam Regular and Bold
make qa-multiscript  # fontbakery on the four new Regular/Bold families
```

`make kamalam` remains as a deprecated alias for the old v1.000 target name.

### Source layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `tools/kallar.py` | The aperture engine, Malayalam build, spectrum, instances |
| `tools/multiscript.py` | The Devanagari/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada build driver |
| `tools/specimen.py` | Malayalam proof images and brand mockups |
| `tools/specimen_multiscript.py` | Multiscript hero, axis and script sheets |

| `tests/test_kallar.py` | Malayalam shaping, variation and colour tests |
| `tests/test_multiscript.py` | Multiscript axes, metadata, coverage and colour tests |

### Reproducible builds

`head.created` and `head.modified` are pinned to a fixed date and
`recalcTimestamp` is disabled. Repeated `make kallar` and `make multiscript`
runs produce byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. `make proofs` is
deterministic too.

## Testing and QA

- HarfBuzz shaping across `APER 0`, `50` and `100` for every script — identical
  glyph sequences and advances, no `.notdef` in any test case.
- Full cmap coverage of each base script, plus conjuncts, matras, reph forms
  and the Devanagari Vedic extensions supported by the base.
- Outline variation at the two extremes, and a guard that Latin stays
  untouched in the script families.
- Static Round/Petal instances differ from each other and carry the correct
  names; COLRv1/CPAL paint graphs are present in every Spectrum build.

  exclusions as Malayalam are used, plus numeric STAT labels that stay inside
  the Windows 31-character limit. Inherited Noto warnings are listed in

- Both HTML specimens and the COLRv1 gradient were verified in headless
  Chromium 156; the shared APER slider drives all four script families.
- Byte-identical repeat builds for `make kallar` and `make multiscript`.

## Design notes

The full design and engineering rationale is in [NOTES.md](NOTES.md),
including:

- why Manjari and Noto Sans are the skeletons;
- the exact aperture parameters for each script;
- why Devanagari needs an absolute headline freeze;
- how the GSUB closure keeps Latin in the base style;

| Script | Profile |
|---|---|
| Malayalam | Full hole-and-crown warp; the original Kallar cut |
| Devanagari | Counters-only below an absolute headline freeze |
| Tamil | Gentler profile concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
| Telugu | Full hole-and-crown warp |
| Kannada | Full hole-and-crown warp |

# Kallar

### A multiscript typeface that blooms.

![Kallar — five scripts, one aperture](proofs/kallar_multiscript.png)

![License: OFL 1.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-OFL%201.1-ee7944)
![Scripts: 5](https://img.shields.io/badge/scripts-5-3d4fbf)
![Variable: APER 0–100](https://img.shields.io/badge/variable-APER%200--100-7f63d6)
![Colour: COLRv1](https://img.shields.io/badge/colour-COLRv1-d973a0)

**Kallar** is a multiscript display type system built around one idea: the
counter as a **lotus gateway**. At one end of its variable axis a loop is the
classic round form; at the other, its crown rises into a soft petal. The
transformation is not a decorative filter — it is a real OpenType variation
axis, interpolated from point-compatible outlines.

The family began with Malayalam and now carries the same `APER` axis into
**Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali), Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**. Each
script is a separate variable family because its shaping, glyph set and
vertical metrics are its own; together they share one axis, one set of design
stops, one Spectrum palette and one build pipeline.

## The idea

Malayalam is a script of loops. The loop head is its most recognisable
gesture: a round counter, an opening, a tail. Most typefaces treat that loop
as a circle or an oval. Kallar treats it as a **gateway**.

At `APER 0` the counter is a classic round loop. As `APER` rises, the crown of
the counter lifts into a soft point: the negative space becomes a lotus petal,
a temple doorway. The outer silhouette follows with a gentler version of the
same gesture, so open arches and closed loops share one rhythm. The counters
themselves change shape — this is outline variation, not a decorative overlay.

The second layer is colour. **Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange
gradient inside the font with COLRv1 and CPAL. The gradient is defined once per
glyph in font units, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than
a set of separately coloured letters.

Kallar is a **display** companion, designed to be set large where the petal
crowns and the spectrum are visible. It is also comfortable in short text,
where the crowns settle into a quiet, readable rhythm.

### Design principles

1. **The counter is the signature.** The transform starts in the negative
   space, not on the outer contour.
2. **One grammar, five scripts.** Scripts keep their own shaping and
   proportions, but share the same aperture logic.
3. **Point compatibility over effects.** Masters only move existing points, so
   every intermediate value is a designed shape and text keeps its metrics.
4. **Colour is part of the type.** The spectrum is painted by the font, not
   pasted on top of it.
5. **Honest derivatives.** The base skeletons, their authors and their OFL
   licences are recorded in the fonts and in this repository.

## Five scripts, one aperture

| Script | Family | Base skeleton | Script codepoints | Glyphs |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Malayalam | `Kallar` | Manjari | full block | 918 / 912 |
| Devanagari (Hindi) | `Kallar Devanagari` | Noto Sans Devanagari | 201 | 1117 |
| Tamil | `Kallar Tamil` | Noto Sans Tamil | 72 | 576 |
| Telugu | `Kallar Telugu` | Noto Sans Telugu | 100 | 1247 |
| Kannada | `Kallar Kannada` | Noto Sans Kannada | 91 | 933 |

“Hindi” is written in Devanagari; the Devanagari family also covers Marathi,
Nepali and Sanskrit. The Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families each cover their
own script plus the Latin, digits and punctuation inherited from the base.

![The APER axis across four scripts](proofs/kallar_multiscript_axis.png)

### Script-specific profiles

Each script has its own aperture profile, because the scripts do not share a
single counter grammar:

- **Devanagari** keeps the shirorekha dead straight. An absolute freeze at the
  headline means only the counters and the loops below it open into petals.
- **Tamil** uses a gentler hole-and-crown profile. Its counters are fewer and
  more open, so the petal is concentrated in the loops and inner curves.
- **Telugu** and **Kannada** take the full hole-and-crown warp. Their round
  loops carry the lotus form most naturally.
- The warp is restricted to the script's **GSUB closure**, so Latin,
  punctuation and unrelated glyphs remain in the base style. The axis changes
  the script's counters, never its glyph sequence, spacing or kerning.

The per-script specimens show the full system:

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Devanagari](proofs/kallar_devanagari.png) | ![Tamil](proofs/kallar_tamil.png) |
| ![Telugu](proofs/kallar_telugu.png) | ![Kannada](proofs/kallar_kannada.png) |

## The APER axis

![The five stops of the aperture axis](proofs/kallar_axis.png)

Every counter in Kallar can open from a classic round loop (`APER 0`) to a
pointed lotus gateway (`APER 100`). The axis has five design stops:

| APER | Name | Character |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Round | The classic loop |
| 25 | Quarter | A first lift at the crown |
| 50 | Bloom | The gateway begins to open |
| 75 | Three-quarters | A clear petal silhouette |
| 100 | Petal | The full lotus display cut (default) |

![The aperture axis in motion](proofs/kallar_aper.gif)

The two masters share the same point topology, so every intermediate value is
a designed shape and HarfBuzz shaping is identical at every stop. The axis
changes the counters and crowns, never the glyph sequence, the spacing or the
kerning.

```css
/* 0 = round · 50 = bloom · 100 = petal */
font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
```

---

## The Spectrum

![Kallar Spectrum](proofs/kallar_gradient.png)

**Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange gradient inside the font itself
with COLRv1 and CPAL. Blue sits at the crown, orange near the baseline and gold
in the descenders, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than a
set of separately coloured letters. Regular and Bold Spectrum builds ship for
every script.

| Stop | Colour | Role |
|---:|---|---|
| 0.00 | `#181E5C` | deep indigo |
| 0.20 | `#2B3FB0` | blue |
| 0.40 | `#5C64DB` | periwinkle |
| 0.58 | `#A06CD2` | violet |
| 0.74 | `#D973A0` | pink |
| 0.88 | `#EE7944` | Sarvam orange |
| 1.00 | `#F9C36D` | warm gold |

Clients with COLRv1 support paint the gradient; clients without it fall back
to the monochrome outlines. The gradient is clipped to each glyph outline and
runs from `y=620` to `y=-120` in font units.

The spectrum is an homage to the lotus-and-gateway visual language of
[Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand). This project is independent and is
not affiliated with or endorsed by Sarvam AI.

## Character set

![Kallar character sheet](proofs/kallar_glyphs.png)

The Malayalam family covers the complete Malayalam block plus Latin:

- 36 consonants, 16 independent vowels, all vowel signs and chillus
- Common conjuncts, reph forms, ya/va post-base signs
- Malayalam digits ൦–൯ and historical numerals ൰–൵
- Rare letters (ഩ ഺ ഽ ൏), chandrabindu, visarga, virama
- Latin uppercase/lowercase, digits, punctuation and common accents
- **918 glyphs** in Regular, **912** in Bold

The multiscript families retain the full cmap and GSUB coverage of their
bases: Devanagari includes the Devanagari block, Devanagari Extended and the
Vedic extensions supported by Noto; Tamil, Telugu and Kannada include their
full blocks. Coverage is verified codepoint by codepoint in
`tests/test_multiscript.py`.

| Family | Script cmap | Colour glyphs (Spectrum) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Kallar (Malayalam) | full block | 913 Regular / 907 Bold |
| Kallar Devanagari | 201 | 1111 |
| Kallar Tamil | 72 | 570 |
| Kallar Telugu | 100 | 1242 |
| Kallar Kannada | 91 | 928 |

## Download

The latest TTF and WOFF2 builds live in [`fonts/`](fonts/). The multiscript
specimen is [`specimen/multiscript.html`](specimen/multiscript.html); the
vector PDF is
[`proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf`](proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf).
Open the HTML directly, or serve both specimens with:

```bash
make serve   # http://localhost:8000
```

For most web projects, use the WOFF2 variable fonts. For desktop design apps,
install the TTF variable fonts. If an app does not expose custom variation
axes, use the static `Round` (APER 0) or `Petal` (APER 100) instances.

> **Note:** the five script families are deliberately separate fonts. There is
> no single merged all-script TTF, because each script has its own GSUB/GPOS
> tables, glyph names and vertical metrics.

## Using Kallar

### Web

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Kallar";
  src: url("Kallar-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400;
  font-display: swap;
}

@font-face {
  font-family: "Kallar";
  src: url("Kallar-Bold.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 700;
  font-display: swap;
}

.bloom {
  font-family: "Kallar";
  font-weight: 700;
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100; /* 0 = round, 100 = petal */
}
```

### Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
  src: url("KallarDevanagari-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400;
}

.deva {
  font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
}
```

### Mixed-script copy

Stack the families. The browser picks the first family that supports each
character — the Malayalam family handles Malayalam and the shared Latin, and
the script families fill in the rest:

```css
.multiscript {
  font-family:
    "Kallar",
    "Kallar Devanagari",
    "Kallar Tamil",
    "Kallar Telugu",
    "Kallar Kannada",
    sans-serif;
  font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
}
```

### Colour

Use `Kallar-SpectrumRegular` / `Kallar-Spectrum`, or the corresponding
`Kallar<Script>-Spectrum*` builds. Clients with COLRv1 support paint the
gradient; clients without it fall back to the monochrome outlines.

```css
.spectrum {
  font-family: "Kallar Spectrum", "Kallar", sans-serif;
  font-weight: 700;
}
```

### JavaScript

```js
const title = document.querySelector(".bloom");
title.style.fontVariationSettings = '"APER" 65';
```

### HarfBuzz

```python
import uharfbuzz as hb

blob = hb.Blob.from_file_path("KallarDevanagari-Regular.ttf")
face = hb.Face(blob)
font = hb.Font(face)
font.set_variations({"APER": 65})
```

### The APER value

| Value | Use it for |
|---:|---|
| 0 | A conventional, round text cut |
| 25–50 | A subtle display lift |
| 50–75 | A clear petal silhouette |
| 100 | The full lotus display cut (default) |

## Building from source

The build is Python + fontTools + varLib + COLRv1.

```bash
make venv            # create .venv and install dependencies
make kallar          # Malayalam: masters, variable fonts, Spectrum, instances
make multiscript     # Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families
make test            # shaping, variation and colour tests for all five scripts
make proofs          # specimen PNGs, GIF and both interactive HTML specimens
make pdf             # Malayalam vector PDF specimen
make pdf-multiscript # multiscript vector PDF specimen
make qa              # fontbakery on Malayalam Regular and Bold
make qa-multiscript  # fontbakery on the four new Regular/Bold families
```

`make kamalam` remains as a deprecated alias for the old v1.000 target name.

### Source layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `tools/kallar.py` | The aperture engine, Malayalam build, spectrum, instances |
| `tools/multiscript.py` | The Devanagari/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada build driver |
| `tools/specimen.py` | Malayalam proof images and brand mockups |
| `tools/specimen_multiscript.py` | Multiscript hero, axis and script sheets |
| `tools/specimen_html.py` | Self-contained Malayalam HTML specimen |
| `tools/specimen_multiscript_html.py` | Self-contained multiscript HTML specimen |
| `tools/pdf.py` | Chromium PDF printer |
| `sources/base/` | Manjari and Noto Sans source fonts + upstream OFL texts |
| `tests/test_kallar.py` | Malayalam shaping, variation and colour tests |
| `tests/test_multiscript.py` | Multiscript axes, metadata, coverage and colour tests |

### Reproducible builds

`head.created` and `head.modified` are pinned to a fixed date and
`recalcTimestamp` is disabled. Repeated `make kallar` and `make multiscript`
runs produce byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. `make proofs` is
deterministic too.

---

## Testing and QA

- HarfBuzz shaping across `APER 0`, `50` and `100` for every script — identical
  glyph sequences and advances, no `.notdef` in any test case.
- Full cmap coverage of each base script, plus conjuncts, matras, reph forms
  and the Devanagari Vedic extensions supported by the base.
- Outline variation at the two extremes, and a guard that Latin stays
  untouched in the script families.
- Static Round/Petal instances differ from each other and carry the correct
  names; COLRv1/CPAL paint graphs are present in every Spectrum build.
- Fontbakery universal: **0 FAIL** on all eight multiscript Regular/Bold
  variable fonts. The same documented custom-axis and Bold/`fsSelection`
  exclusions as Malayalam are used, plus numeric STAT labels that stay inside
  the Windows 31-character limit. Inherited Noto warnings are listed in
  [NOTES.md](NOTES.md).
- Both HTML specimens and the COLRv1 gradient were verified in headless
  Chromium 156; the shared APER slider drives all four script families.
- Byte-identical repeat builds for `make kallar` and `make multiscript`.

---

## Design notes

The full design and engineering rationale is in [NOTES.md](NOTES.md),
including:

- why Manjari and Noto Sans are the skeletons;
- the exact aperture parameters for each script;
- why Devanagari needs an absolute headline freeze;
- how the GSUB closure keeps Latin in the base style;
- metrics, reproducibility, fontbakery exclusions and known limits.

The short version:

| Script | Profile |
|---|---|
| Malayalam | Full hole-and-crown warp; the original Kallar cut |
| Devanagari | Counters-only below an absolute headline freeze |
| Tamil | Gentler profile concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
| Telugu | Full hole-and-crown warp |
| Kannada | Full hole-and-crown warp |
